sources.title: Arctic Winter Sea Ice Hits a Record Low, Again - Eos.org
sources.excerpt: significant downward trend that we’ve observed since 1979

reasoning: Satellite data continuously gathered since 1979 by agencies such as NASA, NOAA, and NSIDC confirm a clear, statistically significant long-term decline in Arctic sea ice extent. While short-term year-to-year fluctuations occur, the overall trend across all seasons—especially the September summer minimum—is strongly downward, with substantial loss in ice area, thickness, and age.
